scored_by: agent-vision model via the primary, two passes per asset (A on the exact 8x nearest-neighbour upscale, B on the engine debug sheet), scored after the authoritative-design-intent re-authoring

verdict.note: Seven v2 assets re-authored with authoritative design intent, scored with the unchanged rubric and both faithful views. Mean 3.39 against the 4.0 bar, with eight criterion scores below 3. The pre-track record is preserved byte-for-byte in test/art/scores-before-intent.json (mean 3.69). No score was revised upward to reach the bar; three >1-point pass disagreements are recorded as human tiebreaks, which the rubric treats as metadata and do not alter the mean. The 4.0 exceptional tier was calibrated unreachable in docs/rubric.md; this record does not lower it.

passes.subject: a pixel art potion bottle with a cork stopper

silhouette.why: The bottle shape with neck, flared shoulders, and stopper is instantly recognizable at a glance.

value_separation.why: The dark brown cork, minty green glass, and dark red liquid are distinct, though the liquid sits directly against the glass sides without clear internal depth.

lighting.why: There is no internal shading or light source indicated on the materials; everything is flat local color.

edge_language.why: The pixel stairs and outlines are relatively clean and consistent, though lacking variation between silhouette and inner details.

cluster_discipline.why: Clean pixel art with solid block structures and no random single-pixel noise or confetti.

palette_craft.why: Colors are pleasant and thematic for a potion, but lack step ramps or lighting variation.

passes.subject: potion bottle

silhouette.why: The bottle shape with cork and liquid is instantly recognizable at 1x from its silhouette alone.

value_separation.why: Cork, glass, and brew are distinct, though the glass outline and light green fill share a close value range.

lighting.why: Flat shaded style with solid color fills rather than directional lighting.

edge_language.why: Clean pixel grid lines but minimal internal edge detailing beyond color changes.

cluster_discipline.why: Solid contiguous pixel clusters with no confetti or stray pixels.

palette_craft.why: Limited, harmonious palette fitting the retro aesthetic nicely.

tiebreak.reason: The two passes disagree by two points. The image is flat local colour with no directional cue, which is better than contradictory light (anchor 1) but short of one consistent direction (anchor 3).

silhouette.why: The distinct shapes of blade, crossguard, hilt, and pommel make the sword immediately identifiable by silhouette alone at 1x scale.

value_separation.why: Light blue blade and yellow crossguard separate, but the brown hilt and yellow pommel have similar luminance values without enough contrast.

lighting.why: There is no directional shading or lighting applied to the blade, hilt, or pommel; they are rendered as flat color fills.

edge_language.why: Edges are clean without pixel noise, but there is no differentiation in treatment between silhouette boundaries and internal material divisions.

cluster_discipline.why: Some elements like the single-pixel blade tip and pommel details are very small, though mostly the piece uses solid blocks.

palette_craft.why: Colors are appropriate for a fantasy sword, but the palette lacks internal shading ramps or temperature shifts for depth.

passes.subject: a pixel art warrior character with a sword

silhouette.why: The 1x silhouette in panel C is instantly recognisable as a humanoid figure with a weapon and helmet.

value_separation.why: Torso and arms have good separation, but parts of the dark helmet blend into the dark outline and background in silhouette.

lighting.why: Lighting comes from above with consistent highlight/shadow placement on armor and blade, but the flat helmet reads mostly uniform.

edge_language.why: Outlines are mostly consistent black borders, though some internal details merge directly into the silhouette boundary.

cluster_discipline.why: Fairly clean pixel grouping with minimal confetti, though some small highlight accents break clean clustering on the hilt.

palette_craft.why: Coherent fantasy color palette with distinct ramps for steel, gold, and cloth, though some shadow ramps are a bit muddy.

tiebreak.reason: The two passes disagree by two points. The helmet, torso, legs and separate sword read as an armed figure in the silhouette panel but the limbs are blocky and partly merge with the body.
The helmet gradient and blade highlight share an upper-left direction; the torso is flat, so one mass is shaded against it.

silhouette.why: The rounded lid and rectangular body are clearly readable as a chest shape without color.

lighting.why: There is no directional lighting or shading applied to any of the masses; it is completely flat color blocking.

edge_language.why: The pixel edges are consistent blocky shapes but lack varied treatments for different materials.

cluster_discipline.why: Clean pixel clusters make up the shapes with no random single-pixel confetti.

palette_craft.why: Flat colors lack ramps or gradients, and the hue choices are somewhat arbitrary with limited contrast between main areas.
